blocks.content: Delhi's demography chapter centres on its extraordinary population density and its status as one of the world's largest urban agglomerations - both frequently tested comparative statistics.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's demographic structure highlights a significant youth population, forming a major demographic dividend.
The 2011 Census recorded an overall literacy rate of 74.04%, with male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%.
The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution officially recognizes 22 regional languages.
Kerala ranks highest in both literacy rate (94.0%) and sex ratio (1084 females per 1000 males).
Uttar Pradesh remains the most populous state, while Sikkim is the least populous state in India.

blocks.content: Demography and social composition reflect the dynamic human resource potential and rich linguistic diversity of the nation.

cells: Detail (2011 Census, latest decennial data; NCR-wide figures are estimates)
approx 1.68 crore (16.8 million), 2011 Census - among the most populous of all Indian states/UTs despite its small area
approx 11,300 persons per sq km (2011) - among the highest of any Indian state/UT
approx 868 females per 1,000 males (2011) - below the national average
approx 97-98% urban - one of the most highly urbanised of all Indian states/UTs
Among the largest urban agglomerations in the world when the wider National Capital Region (including Gurugram, Noida, Faridabad, Ghaziabad) is included

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Delhi's population DENSITY (not just total population) is one of the most repeated superlative facts - among the highest of any Indian state/UT, a direct consequence of its small area combined with very high population.

items: Hindi is the most widely spoken language and Delhi's principal official language, alongside English, Punjabi and Urdu, which also hold official-language status in the NCT under the Official Languages Act applicable to Delhi.

Delhi's population is remarkably diverse and cosmopolitan, drawing migrants from every Indian state given its role as national capital, economic hub, and centre of higher education/government employment - a demographic pattern distinct from more linguistically/culturally homogeneous states.

Major religious communities include Hindus (majority), Muslims, Sikhs (with a particularly strong post-Partition Punjabi-Sikh community presence), Christians, Jains and Buddhists, reflecting the city's layered migration history covered in Chapter 3.
Census 2011 Metrics: Always remember the national sex ratio (943), literacy rate (74.04%), and density (382 per sq km).
8th Schedule Languages: 22 officially recognized languages; Hindi is spoken by the largest percentage of the population, followed by Bengali.
Demographic Extremes: Highest literacy & sex ratio (Kerala); Lowest literacy (Bihar); Highest density (Bihar among states, Delhi among UTs).
Delhi (NCT) population approx 1.68 crore (2011); among the highest population DENSITY of any Indian state/UT (~11,300/sq km).
approx 97-98% urban - one of India's most highly urbanised states/UTs.
Official languages: Hindi, English, Punjabi, Urdu.
Delhi-NCR (including Gurugram, Noida, Faridabad, Ghaziabad) ranks among the world's largest urban agglomerations.
